    Representation-finite Roiter consequences for a critical spine #

    This file removes the former Roiter typeclass premise from the critical-path propagation results and records the full outer composites obtained in BGRS 4.3(a).

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.BGRSCriticalPathSpine.initial_full_outer_spans {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {A : Type v} [Ring A] [Algebra k A] [Module.Finite k A] {ι : Type x} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (S : SplitBasicIdempotents) [HasBGRSDistributiveHomStructure k S.ProjectiveCategory] (hfinite : MildAlg k A) {i j : RayVertex S.RayCategory} {p : Quiver.Path i j} (spine : BGRSCriticalPathSpine p) :
    twoSidedEndomorphismSpan k (spine.lift.pathMap (spine.middle.comp spine.last.toPath)) = ⊤ ∧ twoSidedEndomorphismSpan k (spine.lift.representative spine.first) = ⊤

    At the initial critical cut, both the long suffix and the first arrow generate their complete primitive-projective Hom spaces.

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.BGRSCriticalPathSpine.terminal_full_outer_spans {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {A : Type v} [Ring A] [Algebra k A] [Module.Finite k A] {ι : Type x} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (S : SplitBasicIdempotents) [HasBGRSDistributiveHomStructure k S.ProjectiveCategory] (hfinite : MildAlg k A) {i j : RayVertex S.RayCategory} {p : Quiver.Path i j} (spine : BGRSCriticalPathSpine p) :
    twoSidedEndomorphismSpan k (spine.lift.representative spine.last) = ⊤ ∧ twoSidedEndomorphismSpan k (spine.lift.pathMap (spine.first.toPath.comp spine.middle)) = ⊤

    At the terminal critical cut, both the last arrow and the long prefix generate their complete primitive-projective Hom spaces.

    The two long outer composites denoted delta alpha_n and alpha_1 delta in BGRS 4.3(a) are full Hom generators.

    theorem LargeIndecomposable.BGRSCriticalPathSpine.middle_full_span {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {A : Type v} [Ring A] [Algebra k A] [Module.Finite k A] {ι : Type x} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (S : SplitBasicIdempotents) [HasBGRSDistributiveHomStructure k S.ProjectiveCategory] (hfinite : MildAlg k A) {i j : RayVertex S.RayCategory} {p : Quiver.Path i j} (spine : BGRSCriticalPathSpine p) :
    twoSidedEndomorphismSpan k (spine.lift.pathMap spine.middle) = ⊤

    The middle composite delta of BGRS 4.3(a) itself generates its complete primitive-projective Hom space. Compare it with a full generator mu. If mu allows transit, the full suffix forces the target coefficient to be a unit; if it allows cotransit, the full prefix forces the source coefficient to be a unit.

    theorem LargeIndecomposable.BGRSCriticalPathSpine.middle_not_factors_through_terminal {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {A : Type v} [Ring A] [Algebra k A] [Module.Finite k A] {ι : Type x} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (S : SplitBasicIdempotents) [HasBGRSDistributiveHomStructure k S.ProjectiveCategory] (hfinite : MildAlg k A) {i j : RayVertex S.RayCategory} {p : Quiver.Path i j} (spine : BGRSCriticalPathSpine p) :
    ¬∃ (u : spine.rightInner.obj.as ⟶ j.obj.as) (v : j.obj.as ⟶ spine.leftInner.obj.as), spine.lift.pathMap spine.middle = CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp u v

    The middle composite delta does not factor through the terminal outer vertex a of BGRS 4.3(a). Such a factorization would make the full suffix a left-endomorphism multiple through the last irreducible arrow. Fullness forces that endomorphism to be a unit, while the arrow makes it radical.

    theorem LargeIndecomposable.BGRSCriticalPathSpine.middle_allowsBitransit {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {A : Type v} [Ring A] [Algebra k A] [Module.Finite k A] {ι : Type x} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (S : SplitBasicIdempotents) [HasBGRSDistributiveHomStructure k S.ProjectiveCategory] (hfinite : MildAlg k A) {i j : RayVertex S.RayCategory} {p : Quiver.Path i j} (spine : BGRSCriticalPathSpine p) :
    AllowsTransit (spine.lift.pathMap spine.middle) ∧ AllowsCotransit (spine.lift.pathMap spine.middle)

    The complete middle composite delta allows both transit and cotransit. Every arrow occurrence in the middle has the unconditional representation- finite bitransit property, and both properties are preserved by composition.

    theorem LargeIndecomposable.BGRSCriticalPathSpine.initial_parameter_sandwich_ne_zero {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {A : Type v} [Ring A] [Algebra k A] [Module.Finite k A] {ι : Type x} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (S : SplitBasicIdempotents) [HasBGRSDistributiveHomStructure k S.ProjectiveCategory] (hfinite : MildAlg k A) {i j : RayVertex S.RayCategory} {p : Quiver.Path i j} (spine : BGRSCriticalPathSpine p) (P : ClosedZigzagTransfer.OrientedRadicalPowerParameter spine.leftInner.obj.as) :
    CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (spine.lift.pathMap (spine.middle.comp spine.last.toPath)) P.tau.asHom) (spine.lift.representative spine.first) ≠ 0

    Every oriented generator of the left-inner radical has a nonzero initial endpoint sandwich. Roiter's alternative kills the square of that radical in the endpoint sandwich. The special-zero witness is therefore in the first radical layer, where any oriented parameter differs from it only by a scalar modulo the radical square.

    In the factor branch sigma = lambda delta, the opposite cycle delta lambda survives the first radical layer at the right-inner vertex. If it belonged to the radical square, Roiter's terminal square alternative would annihilate the nonzero initial sandwich of sigma.
